clue.text: Corrected document in legitimate arrest and stated why

parts.note: fair means legitimate, as in fair play
to cop someone is to arrest them

indicators.note: stated means spoken out loud, so the next word gives a letter by its sound

parts.note: the word why, spoken, sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A revised document turns up in the middle of a lawful arrest, with the reasons given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'and' are link words; 'stated' says the word why is heard, giving the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean copy is a neatly written version of a document after its corrections are made.

clue.text: Rising, having consumed fine cheese

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: consumed means ate
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on a pencil grade

explanation.surface: A cheese that rises after swallowing a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole run ATEF upwards, giving the Greek cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: States bordering Illinois briefly in dark

parts.note: Indiana and Kentucky border Illinois; 'briefly' asks for their postal abbreviations IN and KY
Indiana and Kentucky border Illinois; 'briefly' asks for their postal abbreviations IN and KY

explanation.surface: Neighbouring states of Illinois, in short, are kept in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two pieces: the US postal codes for Indiana and Kentucky, two states that border Illinois.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky describes something black or very dark, like ink itself.

clue.text: Opera singer caught by Henry, one with a number not familiar to public

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
the Roman numeral I is one
a PIN is a personal identification number kept secret from everyone else

explanation.surface: An opera singer is nabbed by Henry, who has a song nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'with' are link words. Feodor Chaliapin was a celebrated Russian bass.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaliapin was a famous Russian operatic bass singer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Real patriots after revolution?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things upside down, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Are the true patriots those who come after the uprising?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the working classes as the true patriots in a Marxist revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Proletariats are working classes, who in Marxist theory take power after revolution.

clue.text: Replaced caps, i.e. tops

indicators.note: replaced here means placed again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Caps that have been changed, that is to say tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Apices are the highest points or tips of things, plural of apex.

clue.text: Part of duet that's right and proper, nothing more

parts.note: prim means formally correct and proper
O is nothing, coming as the one more letter at the end

explanation.surface: One half of a musical duo, correct and decent, with nothing extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet, primo is the upper part, played by the first pianist.

clue.text: Dispute with Poe's visitor in tale

indicators.note: in places the visitor inside the word for a tale

parts.note: a conte is a short tale, from the French
in Poe's poem The Raven, a raven comes visiting the narrator

explanation.surface: An argument with the bird that called on Poe in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'in' places the bird inside the French-derived word for a story, just before its final letter. Poe's poem has a raven tapping at the chamber door.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a claim is to contradict or deny it, so to dispute it.

clue.text: View surrealist paintings with ecstasy or shock

parts.note: to scan is to look over or view
works by the surrealist Salvador Dali are Dalis
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Looking at surreal pictures while high on drugs, or out of sheer shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To scandalise people is to outrage or shock them by improper behaviour.

clue.text: What to do before or after violin solo?

definitions.text: What to do before or after violin solo?

parts.words: What to do before or after violin solo?
parts.note: a violinist picks up the bow to play before, and acknowledges applause by bowing after

explanation.surface: Etiquette for a violinist around a solo performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a bow means bending to acknowledge applause, and also picking up the violin's stick.

clue.text: Republic's capital opposed to one monarch's return

parts.note: V is short for versus, against or opposed to
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: return means the queen's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne was a British queen regnant

explanation.surface: The capital of a republic stands against a queen coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the queen's name backwards, giving ENNA, which follows the versus and one pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, which is a republic.

clue.text: Medic, otherwise a part of 25

parts.note: Stevenson's physician whose other self is the first word of the 25 across answer, Hyde

explanation.surface: A doctor who is also a section of a big London park.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is HYDE PARK; its first part names the physician's evil alter ego in Stevenson's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's doctor transforms into Mr Hyde, his alternative personality.

clue.text: Long respected home routine worked out by daughter

indicators.note: worked out means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A domestic routine long respected, devised by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; the rearranged HOME ROUTINE is followed by D.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-honoured means respected because of long tradition.

clue.text: Main reason for warmth towards Europe from America

definitions.text: Main reason for warmth towards Europe from America

parts.words: Main reason for warmth towards Europe from America
parts.note: main is the open sea; the clue reads as friendly feelings but means an ocean current carrying heat across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Why America feels so friendly towards Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it is the old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm Atlantic current flows from the Gulf of Mexico towards Europe, keeping it mild.

clue.text: Constant supporter in game

indicators.note: in puts the supporter inside the game

parts.note: chess is a board game
an angel is a financial backer of a show

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Changeless means unvarying, which is what constant means.

clue.text: Square containing a French joint

parts.note: un is French for a
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A town square holding a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Square in slang means conventional and old-fashioned, the opposite of cool.

clue.text: Valentino's strange and unorthodox work

indicators.note: strange means oddly altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Valentino's peculiar, unconventional creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel is a work of fiction that rejects the traditional novel's conventions.

clue.text: Sleeping, finally, in the raw, when this is misplaced?

definitions.text: Sleeping, finally, in the raw, when this is misplaced?

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of the word sleeping

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps naked because the pyjamas have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: G, the last letter of 'Sleeping', joins IN THE RAW and all nine letters are rearranged; the clue describes why one sleeps naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing worn in bed, the thing missing if one sleeps naked.

clue.text: Businessman at home occupying more ornate surroundings

indicators.note: occupying means the home word sits inside the ornate word

parts.note: fancier means more ornate, here the outer piece
in means at home

explanation.surface: A businessman at home in grander surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier is a person who manages or provides money for business ventures.

clue.text: Information American put together for branch of family

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
US is short for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: Intelligence about Americans compiled for family history.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a subdivision of a family, grouping related species.

clue.text: Score high on visual acuity

parts.note: a score is twenty; a top result on an eye test is expressed as twenty over twenty

explanation.surface: Doing well in an eye test.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal sharp eyesight is described by this figure from the Snellen eye chart.

clue.text: Dance tune initially transmitted by radio

definitions.meaning: the first letter of tune, T, as spoken in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance tune first played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom dance, and also the radio code word for T.

clue.text: He composed a friendly address

definitions.meaning: a composer, Johann Sebastian, of the Baroque era
a Welsh term of endearment, like dear or mate

explanation.surface: A man who wrote a warm letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wales 'bach' is an affectionate way of addressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: J. S. Bach was a German composer; bach is also a Welsh endearment.

clue.text: Following oblique course in southern garden suburb

parts.note: Kew is a London suburb known for Kew Gardens

explanation.surface: Taking a winding route through a leafy south London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. Kew is the west London district home to the Royal Botanic Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: To skew is to move obliquely or at an angle, veering off course.

clue.text: Players are sent off in this direction

definitions.text: Players are sent off in this direction

parts.words: Players are sent off in this direction
parts.note: players are actors and the direction is a stage direction telling them to leave

explanation.surface: Footballers being sent off by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sport; they are actors, and the 'direction' is a stage direction meaning they go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several actors leave the stage.

clue.text: Shelter, say, with explorer in West End area

indicators.note: say signals that the word for shelter is taken by its sound

parts.note: a hide is a shelter for watching birds
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of Africa

explanation.surface: A refuge, as it were, with an explorer in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'in' are link words. Hyde Park is a large royal park in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: This large royal park lies at the western edge of London's West End.

clue.text: Married a Northerner, lucky thing!

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at having married a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: Churchman briefly cut biographical verse

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a cleric is a churchman
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A clergyman shortens his comic poem about a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' removes the final C of CLERIC, leaving CLERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a humorous four-line verse about a famous person.
